title: Fed reaction-function delta: weak payroll headline does not imply immediate policy easing
net_new_delta: After September payrolls rose only 29,000 and unemployment reached 4.2%, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said the report was consistent with ongoing hiring trends, citing roughly 41,000 average monthly job gains over the past year, and said there is still time to assess policy before the late-October meeting. This materially refines ICARUS's labor-softening state: weak payroll growth is confirmed, but at least one hawkish Fed policymaker does not interpret it as requiring an immediate policy response.

FACT: September U.S. payrolls rose 29,000 and unemployment was 4.2%.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said there is still time to assess policy before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.
SOURCE_CLAIM: Hammack said the employment report was consistent with ongoing hiring trends and cited about 41,000 average monthly job gains over the past year as consistent with her estimate for labor-market stability.
Reuters reported no rate move is currently anticipated at the October meeting while the Fed has signaled the possibility of another increase before year-end.
MODEL_INFERENCE: Retain US_LABOR_SOFTENING but reduce confidence that the 29,000 payroll headline alone signals demand collapse or forces immediate Fed easing.
Separate labor-level evidence from the Fed reaction function: weak employment growth can coexist with policy patience when inflation risks remain elevated.
UNKNOWN: Whether other FOMC participants share Hammack's labor-market interpretation.
Whether October inflation and labor data change the late-October policy decision.
Whether low payroll growth reflects labor-demand deterioration, labor-supply constraints, or both.

affected_assumptions: A weak payroll headline should not be mapped mechanically to immediate Fed easing.
ICARUS should model labor-state evidence separately from the Fed reaction function and inflation constraint.
conflicts: Payroll growth of 29,000 and unemployment at 4.2% support labor softening, while Hammack characterizes the trend as consistent with labor-market stability and sees no urgency to decide policy immediately.
next_decisive_check: Compare the next inflation release, weekly claims and subsequent FOMC communication with 2Y yield and October/December policy pricing. A renewed rise in hike probability despite persistently weak payroll/claims evidence would strengthen the inflation-constrained reaction-function state; broad labor deterioration plus falling inflation would weaken it.

evidence.title: Fed's Hammack tells PBS there's still time to weigh next monetary policy move

oracle.finding: Retain labor softening but separate it from the Fed reaction function: the weak September payroll headline does not, by itself, establish demand collapse or an immediate easing response.

supermesh_x.finding: Fresh Reuters/Fed commentary adds a policy-reaction evidence channel distinct from payroll data and market pricing; preserve those provenance classes independently and do not infer consensus from one policymaker.
